title: 1951–52 National Hurling League
text:
{{Short description|21st season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1951–52 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 30 September 1951 – 18 May 1952 |teams = |team1 = Tipperary |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 4th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |previous = [[1950–51 National Hurling League|1950–51]] |next = [[1952–53 National Hurling League|1952–53]] }} The '''1951–52 National Hurling League''' was the 21st season of the [[National Hurling League]]. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |image = |season=1951-52 |winners=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]
4th National League title
Captain: [[Pat Stakelum]] |relegated= |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer= |best goalkeeper= |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1950–51 National Hurling League|1950–51]] |nextseason=[[1952–53 National Hurling League|1952–53]] |updated=19 March 2017 }} The National Hurling League saw a major restructuring for the 1951-52 season. The old system of a four-group National League was abolished. Division 1 was split into two different groups of seven teams. The top-placed team in each group contested the home final. [[Galway GAA|Galway]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1950-51 National Hurling League|1950-51 season]]. On 18 May 1952, [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] won the title after a 6-14 to 2-5 win over [[New York GAA|New York]] in the final. It was their 4th league title overall and their first since [[1949-50 National Hurling League|1949-50]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling
